commits.edited_message:
lib|tests: Replace assert with runtime overflow check in expat_realloc

In expat_realloc, the size passed to realloc_fcn is calculated as
sizeof(size_t) + EXPAT_MALLOC_PADDING + size. Previously, expat_realloc
relied on an assertion:
assert(SIZE_MAX - sizeof(size_t) - EXPAT_MALLOC_PADDING >= size);
under the assumption that preceding accounting checks and parser
invariants preclude reaching an overflow state in practice.

However, in release builds compiled with NDEBUG, assertions are
compiled out. Replace the assert with an explicit runtime check:
if (size > SIZE_MAX - sizeof(size_t) - EXPAT_MALLOC_PADDING) {
  return NULL;
}
immediately preceding the addition, ensuring consistent defensive
behavior across all build configurations.

Also factor the free-space geometry of the input buffer out of the
reparse-deferral heuristic in callProcessor() into a new helper
bufferSpaceAvailable() so that it can be reused by upcoming input
validation work.

Also extend test_alloc_tracker_size_recorded in alloc_tests.c to
exercise SIZE_MAX and SIZE_MAX / 2 with expat_realloc, verifying
that the allocation fails and the recorded size remains unchanged.

Signed-off-by: Filippo Tedeschi <filippotedeschi98@gmail.com>
Co-Authored-By: Claude Code <noreply@anthropic.com>

lib|tests: Validate len against buffer capacity in XML_ParseBuffer

In XML_ParseBuffer(), if len exceeds the space available in the
internal buffer, parser->m_bufferEnd was previously advanced past
parser->m_bufferLim.  This violated the parser's internal pointer
invariant (m_bufferEnd <= m_bufferLim) and caused callProcessor() to
read unallocated or uninitialized heap memory beyond the buffer bounds.

Validate len against bufferSpaceAvailable() for both XML_INITIALIZED
and XML_PARSING states.  If len exceeds the available buffer space,
return XML_STATUS_ERROR with XML_ERROR_INVALID_ARGUMENT.

Also add test_parse_buffer_exceeds_buffer in tests/basic_tests.c.

Co-authored-by: Sebastian Pipping <sebastian@pipping.org>
Signed-off-by: Filippo Tedeschi <filippotedeschi98@gmail.com>
Co-Authored-By: Claude Code <noreply@anthropic.com>

coupling:
Commit 48079b4 (edited) extracts a new helper bufferSpaceAvailable() from the reparse-deferral heuristic in callProcessor(). For that heuristic the helper's definition -- (m_bufferPtr - m_buffer) + (m_bufferLim - m_bufferEnd), i.e. bytes waiting to be parsed PLUS the free tail -- is correct, because the heuristic only needs a conservative estimate of total room before a reallocation, and the XML_CONTEXT_BYTES margin is still subtracted by the caller exactly as before. The commit is benign: the heuristic result is bit-identical to the original, and nothing else uses the helper.
Commit 6154619 (edited) adds its new XML_ParseBuffer() length validation as 'if ((size_t)len > bufferSpaceAvailable(parser))' instead of the strict 'len > EXPAT_SAFE_PTR_DIFF(m_bufferLim, m_bufferEnd)'. Read in isolation this looks like an accurate check of 'available buffer space', and it passes the commit's own test (test_parse_buffer_exceeds_buffer) because that test uses len=10000 against a 2048-byte buffer. But whenever previously-consumed bytes are still sitting in the buffer (m_bufferPtr > m_buffer, which happens after any XML_ParseBuffer() call that ended on a partial token), the helper over-counts the free tail by exactly (m_bufferPtr - m_buffer). A follow-up XML_ParseBuffer() with m_bufferLim-m_bufferEnd < len <= (m_bufferPtr-m_buffer)+(m_bufferLim-m_bufferEnd) is then wrongly accepted: m_bufferEnd advances past m_bufferLim, and callProcessor() hands the tokenizer an [start,end) range that extends beyond the heap allocation, producing a deterministic out-of-bounds read (ASan: heap-buffer-overflow READ in normal_scanComment via XML_ParseBuffer -> callProcessor -> epilogProcessor).
Neither commit alone exhibits the defect: with only 48079b4's edit the strict inline check in XML_ParseBuffer still rejects the oversized len; with only 6154619's edit the code does not even reference a symbol that exists on the base tree (bufferSpaceAvailable is introduced by the other commit), and given a correct helper the check is sound. A reviewer of 48079b4 sees a provably behavior-preserving refactor; a reviewer of 6154619 sees a validation whose correctness depends entirely on the semantics of a helper defined in a different commit. A fix therefore requires cross-commit reasoning: either the validation must use the true free tail (m_bufferLim - m_bufferEnd), or the helper must be redefined/split so it cannot be mistaken for the append capacity -- no single-diff change that preserves both commits' stated maintenance removes the bug.
